# Native retrieval comparison

Both fresh native Codex sessions received the same four retrieval questions, the same frozen knowledge release `2026-10-22.2`, and high effort. Inputs/runtime hashes, exact submitted prompt, native session IDs, full answers and measurements are retained beside this report. Later Q18 recipe improvements and the image-only v3 route did not enter these two runs.

| Condition | Native task wall time | Input tokens | Cached input | Uncached input | Output tokens | Tool invocations | Retrieved case coverage |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| GPT-6-Luna / high | 64.911 s | 359,414 | 304,128 | 55,286 | 6,004 | 8 | 3 complete, B4 partial |
| GPT-6.1-Sol / high | 193.317 s | 258,649 | 206,720 | 51,929 | 6,038 | 5 | 4 complete |
| GPT-6-Luna / high + native Jev-1.14 | 488.219 s | 2,300,434 | 2,161,920 | 138,514 | 46,660 | 28 | 3 core complete, B4 partial; output keys fail contract |

Input totals sum native-reported model requests, including repeated cached context. They are not unique document tokens. Output includes reasoning tokens; do not add reasoning a second time. Dispatch-to-completion wall times are 65.338 s and 193.666 s respectively. Active reasoning/tool/wait intervals and subscription USD remain unknown.

Luna correctly found the equation-spacing history, mark provenance and official equation API. It identified Q18's selected-block transfer and the clipboard limit but did not establish all descendant counts or find the unsupported HWPX string path and its file-based alternative. Sol found those details in the pinned authoring guidance and official support reference. Grading is an evidence-based smoke readback by the knowledge-space producer, not an independently calibrated canonical EvalRun.

The corrective knowledge change exposes the Q18 facts as typed behavior states in `P-native-transfer`: observed HWPML2X transfer and counts, not-exercised OS clipboard, unsupported HWPX strings in the cited native source, and a separately documented `FileSaveBlock_S`/`InsertFile` route. This fixes retrieval structure without changing the retained experiment results.

This one batch supports a narrow observation: Luna finished sooner; Sol used fewer reported input tokens and retrieved more complete evidence. It establishes neither a general model ranking nor the knowledge space's causal savings, because there is no matched unstructured-history baseline.

The user authorized and completed a fresh Luna/high + native Jev-1.14 treatment on the same four cases. Its original release/runtime is separately frozen under `jev-treatment/frozen-space`. All 32 installed families were reviewed; 19 produced decisions where applicable. Three actual provider requests returned 30 decision records containing 68 primitive answers. There were 28 native source-record applications, including three later superseded source-occurrence selections; 25 applications remain non-superseded. Application receipts and downstream use are separately recorded in `jev-treatment/consumption.actual.json`. Provider-reported Jev cost totals **USD 0.001153530**, with 27,465 input and 1,831 output tokens. Native Luna subscription USD is unknown, so this is not the whole treatment price.

The treatment used eight knowledge retrieval invocations plus 59 native protocol command invocations inside 28 actual Codex tool calls. It took 488.219 seconds of native task wall time (488.559 from dispatch), 7.52 times this Luna baseline; uncached input was 2.51 times the baseline. Extra protocol instructions, source corrections, setup and native failures are part of this maximal-intervention condition. One sequential trial with those differences cannot isolate a causal Jev effect.

The B4 context shortlist supplied only `S-bindingsF`, `S-copyF` and unrelated feedback. It omitted `S-guidanceF` and the official discussion containing the unsupported HWPX strings and file alternative. Jev could not select evidence absent from the supplied candidates. Three source-find candidates also had producer-authored descriptions pointing to the wrong lines (13/22/25 instead of 9/16/17); raw readback caught this and fresh corrected decisions superseded them. A separate exposure limit hid the font hash from the worker's filtered view although it exists in the full frozen metric snapshot. These findings motivate exact occurrence validation and per-question evidence-facet coverage before semantic selection.

Actual Jev bindings remained the inherited **Root native actor**, while a separately observed Luna session consumed the decisions. This is not an independently bound Luna Jev actor. One hierarchy decision had no native action; one continuation decision failed native application with `JEV_NATIVE_BOUNDARY_NOT_OBSERVED`. A fresh disposition request was denied `STORAGE_INTEGRITY` before provider submission. No paid replay, accounting repair, alternate sender or fabricated actor identity was attempted. The final answer also used `evidence`/`limits` instead of required `recordIds`/`evidencePaths`/`limitations`; raw outputs remain unchanged and do not pass the response contract.

This trial establishes no coverage gain from maximal Jev intervention. It identifies candidate coverage/integrity and runtime identity/application problems worth fixing independently. Successor knowledge adds typed evidence states, exact occurrence checks, evidence-facet gap detection and routing guidance. Those changes were not retroactively included in the frozen runs. Read `jev-treatment/measurements.actual.json` and `jev-treatment/audit.actual.json` for exact receipts and limits; no general Jev/model ranking or knowledge-space savings is claimed.
